sections.h2: A large county with several markets
sections.html: Miami-Dade covers 1,899.90 square miles and had an estimated 2,802,029 residents in mid-2025. It holds 1,125,274 housing units, and 52.2 percent are owner-occupied. The typical owned home is valued at $463,000. With roughly half the housing rented, caps and exemptions matter a lot to owners here, and so does the line between an owner-occupied home and a rental.

Three county offices split the work, so match the question to the desk.

  • Property Appraiser: value, exemptions, portability and classifications. The main office is in the Stephen P. Clark Center, 111 NW 1st Street, Suite 710 (305-375-4712). The Cutler Bay branch is at 10710 SW 211 Street, 2nd Floor (305-232-3810). Each is staffed on weekdays during business hours.
  • Tax Collector: prints and collects the bill, with 13 service locations, 24 hour online payment and mobile offices that visit neighborhoods.
  • Clerk of the Courts: records deeds, takes value petitions and runs tax deed auctions.

The appraiser does not send tax bills or set and collect taxes. A complaint about the size of a bill belongs with the taxing bodies that levy millage.

The appraiser's June 1 estimate put countywide taxable value at $540.7 billion, up 5.5 percent from 2025 and 3.2 percentage points slower than the prior year's gain. A July 1 preliminary certification went to the taxing authorities. The County Commission ordered the roll extended on September 1, 2026, and the appraiser certified it on October 16, 2026. That first certification comes before any changes the Value Adjustment Board makes after appeals.

The total comes from stacked taxing bodies, and the city layer varies widely. The 2026 millage chart runs from 14.9007 on one North Miami Beach line to 24.1893 in Biscayne Park, with unincorporated areas at 16.8983. Other totals include Miami at 19.9544, Miami Beach at 18.6681, Hialeah at 18.6134, Coral Gables at 18.1518 and Doral at 16.9487.

The chart lists more than three dozen taxing areas. Looking only at a city's own operating line, Doral is lowest at 1.5994 mills, Hialeah sits mid-range at 6.3018, and Biscayne Park is highest at 9.2000. A low city line can still sit on a heavy total once school, county, fire and library lines are added, and some rows add debt service or special district lines. Match your own address to a row instead of quoting a city figure.

Separate tax guides cover Miami and Miami Beach.

Bills land in November. Payment in November earns the full 4 percent discount, and the discount drops a point each month through February. Anything unpaid on April 1 is delinquent. The Tax Collector promotes the November discount as "Save the Max" and takes payment online, at its 13 locations or at its mobile offices.

  • August: the proposed-tax notice previews the bill.
  • Twenty-five days from that notice: the last chance for a value petition at the clerk's desk.
  • Thirty days after a denial letter is mailed: the window to challenge an exemption denial.
  • May 1: the cutoff for asking the collector for installments.

sections.h2: When a Miami-Dade bill goes unpaid
sections.html:
If a bill stays open, the collector packages it as a tax certificate and auctions it to the bidder willing to earn the least interest, with bids dropping a quarter point at a time. Certificates nobody bids on pass to the county at the top rate, and the sales wrap up by June 1. A homestead parcel owing less than $250 skips the auction and goes to the county. The collector retains a 5 percent commission.

Loss of the house takes longer. The certificate holder waits two years from the April after issue, then pays a $75 application charge. At the later auction the top bidder posts a deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is larger, and settles the rest inside 24 hours on business days. Ask the clerk for auction dates. A seller with an open year should get a payoff early, since the title agent cannot close over a delinquent lien and the balance grows with advertising and interest.

sections.h2: How fast an assessment can climb
sections.html:
Homestead value is held to the smaller of 3 percent and inflation. Rentals, second homes and commercial parcels face a 10 percent annual ceiling. A sale wipes out both cushions, since the new owner is assessed at market the following January 1.

A constitutional amendment that voters approved in November 2026 is already built into the appraiser's estimator, which shows Amendment 3 figures for 2027 and 2028. Run your own folio through it before guessing at a future bill. Millage itself comes out of budget hearings held in the fall.

The base homestead exemption reaches $50,000 and is claimed with the appraiser by March 1. Other breaks target particular owners.

  • Seniors: an extra exemption, as large as $50,000, where a local ordinance provides it and household income stays under the cap.
  • Service-connected disability at 10 percent or higher: a $5,000 reduction.
  • Veteran owners 65 or older with a permanent service-connected disability: a discount equal to the VA rating.
  • Deferral: file Form DR-570 with the tax collector by March 31 to postpone the share of the bill above 5 percent of income, or 3 percent for permanent residents past 65.

Widow(er) exemptions, and disability exemptions for a veteran or surviving spouse, can be filed online, and agricultural classification uses form MD-482 with uploaded papers. Appointments can be booked online, and a tax estimator and walkthrough video sit on the appraiser's home page.

Owners of furniture, equipment and similar business property file Form DR-405 with the appraiser by April 1. The clerk runs a free alert that notifies an owner within a day when a deed or mortgage is filed under that name, and the appraiser's compliance team takes suspected homestead fraud reports at 305-375-3402.

sections.h2: What changes when a Miami-Dade house sells
sections.html:
Your title agent pulls the collector's balance and settles the year's tax at closing, split the way your contract sets out. The buyer arrives with a reassessed value and needs a fresh exemption filing.

Deed stamps are 60 cents per $100. The county adds a 45 cent surtax per $100 that state revenue officials exclude for a deed conveying nothing but a single-family house. Ask the closing agent which line your deed falls under.

Before listing, collect your latest statement, the proposed-tax notice, proof of any exemption on file and a payoff letter for any open year. A cash buyer who takes the property as is can shorten the timeline, but open taxes still come out of your proceeds.

faqs.q: What total millage applies in unincorporated Miami-Dade for 2026?
faqs.a: The chart total is 16.8983 mills for the unincorporated area. Incorporated cities have their own totals.

faqs.q: Where can a Miami-Dade owner pay the bill?
faqs.a: Use the Tax Collector: its website, any of 13 locations or a visiting mobile office. The appraiser takes no payments.

faqs.q: How soon must a Miami-Dade value petition be filed?
faqs.a: Twenty-five days from the August notice of proposed taxes. File the petition with the clerk. A denied exemption follows a 30 day clock from the letter.

faqs.q: Does paying early cut a Miami-Dade bill?
faqs.a: Yes, by up to 4 percent. The reduction shrinks every month from November and is gone by March.

faqs.q: Is Miami-Dade subject to the Save Our Homes limit?
faqs.a: Yes. Homestead growth is limited to the lesser of 3 percent or inflation, and a sale resets it.
